items.stem: Which statements about Rust ownership are true? (Select TWO)

options.text: Each value has exactly one owner at a time
options.rationale: Correct: single ownership is the core rule that enables deterministic cleanup.

options.text: A value is dropped when its owner goes out of scope
options.rationale: Correct: drop runs deterministically at the end of the owner's scope.

options.text: Values are deep-copied on every assignment by default
options.rationale: Non-Copy values are moved, not copied, on assignment.

options.text: A garbage collector frees values at runtime
options.rationale: Rust has no garbage collector; cleanup is scope-based.

items.explanation: Correct: single ownership is the core rule that enables deterministic cleanup.; Correct: drop runs deterministically at the end of the owner's scope.

items.stem: In a function returning `Result<T, E>`, what does the `?` operator do on an `Err`?

options.text: Returns early, propagating the error to the caller
options.rationale: Correct: ? short-circuits and returns the Err from the enclosing function.

options.text: Converts the error to a String and prints it
options.rationale: ? does not print; it returns the error value.
? never discards errors; it returns them.

items.explanation: Correct: ? short-circuits and returns the Err from the enclosing function.
